lines.en: Limited Random Item Box.
According to the lore of ‘Ways of Survival,’ this was a coin item that had been sold as a limited edition in a past ‘scenario.’
[W-wait, wh-why is this here?]
Biryu, who appeared a moment later, also let out a cry of astonishment.
[Th-th-that should have been banned from sale almost immediately!]
According to the original ‘Ways of Survival,’ this item had a fairly complicated backstory.
Released long before the scenario for planetary system 8612 even began, this coin item had been forcibly recalled by the Star Stream’s Bureau.
With good reason: the fact that inserting a ‘lower-tier item’ would always produce a ‘higher-tier item’ had consequences so far-reaching that it threatened the balance of the scenarios.
What was more, a single item box cost a staggering 1 million coins.
The constellations were outraged by this absurd pricing policy, and the stupid dokkaebi who had devised the item was fired from the Bureau.
[C-constellations-nim. That, you seeee······. I don’t really know why that’s there eith······ E-ehehehe! Broadcast over!]
[Channel #BI-7623 is temporarily closing.]
When Biryu vanished after babbling nonsense to himself, the voices of the constellations disappeared as well.
It was a shame I couldn’t see the constellations’ reactions anymore, but, well, what could I do?
Rrrrr.
I looked down at the box, which was vibrating on its own. The random draw was about to begin in earnest.
[A sword-type item was inserted. An item of the same type will appear as the reward!]
[The random draw is beginning!]
The Limited Random Item Box randomly spat out a higher-grade item related to whatever had been put inside.
That meant that, in terms of probability, anything from C-grade to SSS-grade could come out.
In terms of probability, that is.
[The item offered as a sacrifice is associated with a particular constellation!]
[The probability of an item associated with that constellation appearing has increased greatly.]
···Huh?

That was an unexpected message. Still, it didn’t seem likely to work against me. Sweat pooled in my clenched hands. Even buying random-draw items in online games had never made me this nervous. Please, just give me something around A-grade.
[A higher-grade item has appeared!]
[The Random Item Box has 0 uses remaining.]
At last, the box stopped shaking, and the dazzling light subsided.
I glanced at Yoo Sangah and Lee Gilyoung in turn. Their eyes were shining.
“Shall we open it?”
“Yes!”
We opened the box.
“W-woooow!”
Lee Gilyoung’s scream was so loud that it startled even me. But what was inside really was that astonishing.
A pure white blade (劍身) extending from an elegant, ink-black guard······ But didn’t its shape look a little like ‘Broken Faith’?
I immediately checked the item information.
<Item Information>
Name : Unbreakable Faith
Grade : Star Relic (星遺物)

Description : The sword of ‘Kaizenix,’ the hero who led Grunsiad’s Great Magic Age (大魔道時代) in the past. Imbued with Kaizenix’s great mastery over ether, it can create ‘Blades of Faith’ bearing the powers of fire, darkness, and divinity (神聖), respectively.
As an additional effect, equipping it raises Constitution and Strength by 2 levels each.
For a moment, I was speechless.
Wait··· was this for real?
I hadn’t gotten an item with a mere letter grade, but an actual Star Relic (星遺物)?
“D-Dokja-ssi! Even at a glance, that looks like an incredible item!”
It was an incredible item.

In the world of ‘Ways of Survival,’ ‘Star Relics’ were the only items excluded from the grading chart. This wasn’t simply because they had powerful abilities, but because these items were very special.
Every Star Relic held the power a constellation had possessed while alive.

Their capabilities varied enormously depending on the world in which the constellation had been a hero and how widely known that constellation was, but simply containing a constellation’s power gave a Star Relic tremendous value.
And it even raised Constitution and Strength by 2 each.
Considering that even an overall stat boost of just 1 was enough to elevate an item to A-grade, its additional effects alone made it equivalent to at least an S-grade item.
Even Yoo Joonghyuk probably hadn’t obtained an item this good yet.
As a courtesy, I turned toward Yoo Sangah and Lee Gilyoung and asked,
“······It’s all right if I take it, isn’t it?”
“Of course. Naturally, it’s yours, Dokja-ssi.”
Yoo Sangah, insisting as if to settle the matter firmly in advance. Lee Gilyoung was nodding enthusiastically, too.

I glanced at Han Myungoh, but he was merely gnawing on a ground rat’s leg with a vacant expression, muttering something unintelligible as he did. I’d been certain he would spout more nonsense about taking it for himself······ How strange.
[You have acquired a Star Relic.]
[The owner of the Star Relic is curious about you.]
Judging by the message, the constellation apparently still existed somewhere. I would have to open ‘Ways of Survival’ and look it up later.
“Then let’s head back now. There are plenty of ground rats outside, too, so we should be fine just taking the Magic Power Stoves back.”
“But how do we get back?”
“We got here using Gilyoung’s ability, so getting out shouldn’t be a problem. With [Diverse Communication]······.”
But Lee Gilyoung looked troubled.
“Hyung, um······.”
“Hmm?”
“There aren’t any insects nearby.”
Come to think of it, all the insects around us had burst from the pressure during our fight with the Dark Keeper. It was a problem I hadn’t considered.
“Not even one? A few should still be alive. If we move around a little while you use your ability······.”
There were so many insects in the world. Killing a few couldn’t possibly leave none for him to communicate with. But Lee Gilyoung’s expression remained gloomy.
“Well, there actually is one I can call······.”
Lee Gilyoung closed his eyes, murmured something, and began to concentrate.
“Dokja-ssi, something seems wrong with Gilyoung.”
Lee Gilyoung’s eyes were slowly rolling back. And a thin stream of blood trickling from his nose.
“Gilyoung?”
Suddenly, a heavy boom sounded, and a tremor spread from above. Dust sifting down throughout the cave.
This tremor was coming from the surface······.
A chill instantly ran through my entire body.
Booom!
“Gilyoung! Lee Gilyoung! Snap out of it!”
“Uh······, hyung?”
Lee Gilyoung’s rolled-back eyes returned to normal.
“Gilyoung, stop the skill! Hurry!”
Only after a startled Lee Gilyoung stopped his skill did the tremors subside.
I sighed in relief.
Come to think of it, some incredibly dangerous creatures were roaming the surface above us.
Countless high-grade monsters, including the Corpse-Poison Rhinoceros, a grade-7 monster species.
And among those monsters were creatures of the insect king species (蟲王種), whose grade was unknown. As the name suggested, the insect king species was a type of insect.
“You really······.”
I started to say something, then stopped and placed a hand on Lee Gilyoung’s head.
He could actually call a creature of the insect king species from the surface······ What was he, Fabre? We’d nearly been buried alive right here.
“That skill is off-limits for now. Don’t ever use it until I tell you to. Got it?”
“Okaaay······.”
Lee Gilyoung answered dejectedly. That left us no choice but to wait.
“We’ll get lost if we go straight into the Dark Fold. We should wait a little longer and move once some small insects appear nearby.”
Getting in had been easy, but the [Dark Fold] was actually a very dangerous place. Take even a slightly wrong turn, and a day or two could vanish in no time.
Then Yoo Sangah raised her hand.
“Um, if all we need to do is get back, I think I can take Gilyoung’s place.”
I almost asked whether she was planning to have a conversation with the [Dark Fold] this time, but it somehow sounded sarcastic, so I held back. Yoo Sangah spoke with a little uncertainty.
“I have a similar skill, too.”
Come to think of it, I still didn’t know Yoo Sangah’s attribute or constellation sponsor.
“What kind of skill?”
“Well, if I had to explain it, it’s a skill that finds the way using a ball of thread······.”
A ball of thread?
“······Excuse me, but may I ask what your attribute is, Yoo Sangah-ssi?”
Yoo Sangah wasn’t a character in the original novel, so I couldn’t hear her thoughts. Just as I couldn’t hear Lee Gilyoung’s or Han Myungoh’s.
Yoo Sangah looked deeply troubled. If only I could use ‘Character List’ on her, this wouldn’t be so frustrating. As an experiment, I activated ‘Character List’ once more.
[Activating the exclusive skill ‘Character List’!]
[This person is not registered in ‘Character List.’]
As expected······. But there was one more line to the message.
[Information on this person is currently being collected.]
That message hadn’t appeared before.
Come to think of it, I’d briefly heard a system message when Yoo Sangah activated her ‘Interpreter’ skill during the earlier fight.
I hadn’t been able to hear those before.
Could ‘Character List’ update as time passed, too?
No way······.
After sorting through various thoughts, I decided to let the troubled Yoo Sangah off the hook for now.
“I shouldn’t have asked. In any case, you did the right thing. Keep being careful about revealing your attribute information to other people.”
“That’s not it! It isn’t that I don’t trust you, Dokja-ssi······!”
Looking more closely, Yoo Sangah seemed to have something else she wanted to say. A thought suddenly flashed through my mind.
“Did your sponsor say something about me, Yoo Sangah-ssi?”
Yoo Sangah lowered her head, looking close to tears.
“I’m sorry.”

She barely managed the words through trembling lips. At this point, it was likely that her sponsor hadn’t merely said something; she had probably made some sort of oath along with the contract. Revealing information was probably subject to a restriction that put her life at stake.
Whatever constellation it was, it seemed determined to cultivate Yoo Sangah in earnest.
“It’s all right. I understand.”
“Thank you, really······.”

There was no need to thank me. Hearing it directly from her wasn’t the only way to identify her sponsor······ If anything, my heart was pounding with anticipation. A reader’s urge to fill in the blanks between the lines, perhaps.
“Then I’ll try using the skill.”
Soon, something like a faintly glowing thread grew from Yoo Sangah’s fingertips and began to stretch outward.
“Actually, I tied some ‘thread’ and left it behind when I was being abducted earlier, in case this happened.”
One strand led to me, while another led outside. That thread was probably tied to Lee Hyunsung or Jung Heewon.
“Let’s go.”
There was no way Yoo Sangah had possessed a skill like this from the beginning. This was clearly a stigma provided by her sponsor.
But ‘thread’ for escaping a labyrinth.
This······ somehow felt like a constellation I knew.
[Channel #BI-7623 has reopened.]
Once again, I heard messages announcing the constellations’ arrival.
[A few constellations have filed complaints about the channel’s transmission and reception system!]
[The constellation, ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon,’ is curious about what on earth came out of the random box.]
Oh, you didn’t get to see it, did you?
What a shame. Whatever will you do?
[Damn it! That fucking bastard—my channel······ Hahaha! Have you all been well while I was away?]
And a welcome······ no, familiar voice returned.
It was Bihyung.
[······You pulled off some incredible things again while I was gone, huh?]
‘So I was the reason you couldn’t come back all this time?’
[That’s······ well, it wasn’t entirely unrelated. The Bureau gave me a warning for suddenly ending the broadcast and leaving the ads running too long.]

At the moment, only I could hear Bihyung’s voice. This was the so-called ‘Dokkaebi Communication,’ supposedly used only among dokkaebis. Of course, allowing me, an incarnation, to access it was a clear violation of the rules.
[I’ve decided to stop worrying about the little things. I can make a few more trips to the Bureau. More importantly······ how did you know about the ‘random box,’ too?]
‘I just happened to.’
[Damn it. To think there were still remnants of that embarrassing past left. Of all places, why was that box there······.]
‘Embarrassing past?’
‘······Wait. Don’t tell me you were the one who devised that ridiculous coin item?’
Even I, an avid reader of ‘Ways of Survival,’ hadn’t known that.
[Damn it! If only I hadn’t gotten greedy back then······.]
“Wow, this really is delicious.”
Jung Heewon’s exclamation interrupted Bihyung’s grumbling.
Ten minutes earlier, with Yoo Sangah guiding us, we had safely reunited with the rest of the group.
Fortunately, Jung Heewon and Lee Hyunsung had held their position at the boundary until we returned.
“Eating that should restore some of your energy.”
“Mm, I really do seem to be feeling better.”
Jung Heewon experimentally rolled her shoulders, and even at a glance, her complexion had improved considerably. Cooked meat from subterranean species did, in fact, contain detoxifying substances.
“It looks like you got all sorts of things in there. Besides the Magic Power Stoves······.”
“A few things.”
I spoke while looking at Lee Hyunsung.
After repeatedly putting on and taking off the [Old Iron Shield] I’d given him earlier, Lee Hyunsung was now breathing on its surface and polishing it.
Anyone watching would have thought he’d bought a new car.
[The character ‘Lee Hyunsung’ shows a faint sense of loyalty toward you.]
Jung Heewon, who had been watching him with apparent envy, asked,
“Is there anything I could use?”
“No.”
“What about that sword?”
“It’s mine.”
“······You’re going to share the meat with everyone, of course?”
“I’m charging coins for it.”
“You know······ you really are stingy, Dokja-ssi.”
“Let’s say I’m good at staying alive.”
As we traded remarks, each carrying a cooked ground rat, we reached the end of the tunnel before we knew it.
Our surroundings suddenly grew brighter, and people began to come into view. But the atmosphere was a little strange. What was this sense of urgency and frantic activity?
[20 minutes remain until paid settlement.]
[Please prepare your survival fee.]
Only then did I look at the clock and realize.
I see.
Was it that time already?
It was astonishing that the word ‘paid’ could sound this frightening.
“Coins, please give me some coins!”
“My child doesn’t have any coins! Please, some coins······.”
For anyone who had diligently participated in the scenarios, 100 coins or so wouldn’t be a problem. But diligent people were rare to begin with.
“I’ll give you 1 million won—no, 10 million! Somebody sell me just 100 coins!”
The price of coins was skyrocketing.
It was ridiculous.
A currency that had been worthless before the ruin began was now commanding an absurd premium.
And some bastards were watching from a distance, snickering. The ones who already had plenty of coins.
Cheon Inho and the Cheoldoo Group.
Several women crowded around the gang, and I heard them shouting something.
“B-but you clearly said you’d give us 100 coins earlier!”
“Hmm, did I? I don’t remember.”
“I might reconsider if you let me fuck you one more time. How about it?”
Jung Heewon had already drawn her sword and was glaring in their direction.
“Those sons of bitches finally······.”
[The attribute of the character ‘Jung Heewon’ is preparing to bloom.]
It was nearly Jung Heewon’s time, too. Having it bloom now wouldn’t be bad······ but not yet. A little more patience was needed before she could obtain the ‘attribute’ I had in mind.
That was when a system message appeared.
[Survival fee settlement will begin shortly.]
“S-save me! Please save me!”
The members of our group reacted differently to those words. Lee Hyunsung bowed his head as if in anguish, and Jung Heewon bit her lip, sword in hand.
Everyone knew the price of ‘paid settlement.’ There was no one here who hadn’t experienced it.
“······Dokja-ssi.”
And Yoo Sangah looked at me.
“Yes.”
In this world, coins were power.
Those with coins acquired good items. Those with coins acquired good stats.
Those with coins had everything.
[Several more constellations who received scenario recommendations have entered the channel.]
[The constellation, ‘Secretive Plotter,’ is watching your choice.]
[The constellation, ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband,’ is watching your choice.]
[The constellation, ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire,’ is watching your choice.]
And right now, I was the human with the most coins in this station.
Just as I was about to speak, Cheon Inho’s voice reached me.
“Oh, Dokja-ssi! You’ve arrived at just the right time.”
Having spotted us, Cheon Inho was smiling in our direction. Just as an ominous feeling came over me, he continued in a loud voice.
“Come to think of it, you had plenty of coins, Dokja-ssi! How many was it? If I remember correctly, you were the richest among us?”
[The character ‘Cheon Inho’ activates the skill ‘Incite Lv.2’!]
The crowd hastily turned toward me.
“C-coins?”
“Who has lots of coins?”
It didn’t take long for every gaze to settle on me.
Cheon Inho really was impressive when it came to petty schemes.
“D-did you say you were Dokja-ssi?”
“Please save us!”
People approached, panting, and clutched at my trouser legs.
Even a rough count put the number gathering around me at more than 20. If I gave all these people coins, I would lose a staggering 2,000 coins.
But if I didn’t give them any, I would instantly become Geumho Station’s archvillain.
[Your understanding of the character ‘Cheon Inho’ has increased.]
“Haha, Dokja-ssi. I don’t have enough coins to help these poor people······ but you’re different, aren’t you? Are you just going to stand by and watch?”
I sighed quietly.
There were only so many times I would play along with this sort of trick.
[Constellations of the Absolute Good alignment have designated the character Cheon Inho an ‘evil person (惡人).’]
I’d already shown plenty of patience with this small fry.
“S-save us!”
“Please save us!”
People rushing at me, wailing and sobbing, wearing the most pitiful expressions in the world.
[Hahaha! The story is getting interesting. By the way, you have 10 minutes left now!]
Bihyung chattering in a voice brimming with delight, and my companions looking at me, unsure what to do.
I let out a short sigh, slowly closed my eyes, then opened them.
“I see. You want me to give you coins?”
Then I smiled.
“Why should I?”
I looked around at the people.
The first scenario was original sin (原罪) itself. So there was no one innocent among the people here.
That made them all the more disgusting.
People who had trampled someone else to prolong their own lives, yet couldn’t even take responsibility for the lives they had prolonged.
“W-what do you mean, why!”
“You’ve got plenty of coins! Can’t you spare a few?”
Amid the confusion, Cheon Inho burst out laughing.
“I knew you would say that, Dokja-ssi.”

“You’ve been like this ever since you first appeared here, Dokja-ssi. Selling the food you brought for coins, for instance. Do you know how many people could survive now if they hadn’t bought food from you back then?”
“That’s right! He’s right!”
“Fuck! Give me my coins back!”
Before I knew it, it felt as though I was being put on trial.
This was probably the scene Cheon Inho had wanted.
“Wait, everyone! What you’re doing right now······!”
“Dokja-ssi isn’t that kind of person!”
Yoo Sangah and Lee Hyunsung belatedly tried to defuse the situation, but the crowd had already lost all reason. And then Cheon Inho drove in the final nail.
“Dokja-ssi. I’ll give you one last chance. Return their coins.”
“And if I refuse?”
“Then the worst will happen.”
A crowd numbering fully twenty began advancing, one step at a time.
“Y-you······ Hurry! Hurry and hand over the coins!”
Even so, no one readily charged at me first. Finally, a member of the Cheoldoo Group stepped forward, unable to stand watching any longer.
“You fucking morons! What are you doing? Kill him! Just kill him and take the coins. What are you hesitating for?”
The man who swaggered forward shouting was fairly well built. I activated [Character List] to check his information.
<Character Summary List>
Name : Han Minsung
Exclusive Attribute : Thug (General)
Overall Stats : [Constitution Lv.8], [Strength Lv.8], [Agility Lv.8], [Magic Power Lv.2]
He had fairly respectable stats for a thug. There was no way they had been this high to begin with······ So had these bastards really done ‘that’ after all?
Right. He was getting cocky because he trusted his overall stats.
“Die, you bastard!”
The iron pipe in his hand moved. An iron pipe carrying the full force of level-8 Strength. It would have been enough to make the old ‘Kim Dokja’ tremble in fear, but······.
To me now, it was merely laughable.
Shhk!
The man’s arm, severed clean through along with the iron pipe, rolled across the floor.
“Aa-aaargh!”
Stained with human blood, [Unbreakable Faith] sang out, spilling white light. I quietly swept my gaze over the people.
When the Cheoldoo Group member was subdued with a single blow, everyone around me went pale. I’d put on enough of a show. It was time to begin.
“How pathetic······ Do you really believe I’m the reason things have come to this?”
I spoke while studying each face in the crowd, from left to right. Across from me, I could see Cheon Inho’s flustered face.
“You know perfectly well that this isn’t actually my fault.”
The people’s mouths opened and closed like sick goldfish. I continued, as if scattering feed.
“You’re only doing this because you’re scared of them. You know what’s really wrong, and you’re about to die because of it, but here you are, trembling just because you’re scared of those guys.”
“Haha, listen, Dokja-ssi! What are you saying······.”
“Because they’re stronger than you! Because their overall stats are higher, and they have more coins! But do you know something?”
I asked as I took a step toward the crowd. The entire crowd retreated like startled goldfish. But they were already in my fish tank.
“Why are they stronger than you?”
I took another step.
“Why have they always had more coins than you? Because they’re thugs? Please.”
[The surrounding characters are becoming agitated.]
Even amid fear, some emotions spread unmistakably. Questions passing from one face to another.
“C-come to think of it, how did Cheon Inho-ssi get so many coins······?”
“Haha, you all know, don’t you? Well, I’ve sold various things, and also―”
“You think that alone could give him stats that high? Really?”
Cheon Inho shut his mouth. Once again, I looked at the faces in the crowd one by one, this time from right to left, and spoke.
“When I came to Geumho Station a few days ago, there were 87 people here in total.”
“But how many are here now? From what I can see, there are fewer than 50, even at the highest estimate. Do you know why?”
“Th-that’s because they took turns going out to scout in the morning, and the monsters―”
“Monsters? You still believe that?”
“Th-then what on earth······?”
“You idiots. Use your heads and think. Would those people really have died because of monsters? Then why hasn’t a single member of the Cheoldoo Group died?”
Suddenly, everything went quiet.
“And why did those bastards come back stronger?”
[The constellation, ‘Secretive Plotter,’ nods at your powers of deduction.]
“D-don’t tell me―”
One by one, people turned toward Cheon Inho. The Cheoldoo Group members faltering and backing away. Now it was my turn to drive in the nail.
“Those bastards said it earlier. That killing me would give them ‘coins.’”
[The constellation, ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband,’ excitedly pulls out strands of hair.]
“But how on earth did those bastards know that ‘killing people gives you coins’?”
“Y-you people······ Inho-ssi! Surely not?”
“Shut up! It’s a false accusation!”
As Cheon Inho stepped back, members of the Cheoldoo Group drew their weapons one by one. The terrified people let out low groans.
[Hahaha! You have 7 minutes left now!]
I stepped in front of them and spoke.
“If you have any pride left at all, fight with your own hands.”
The Blade of Faith sang fiercely. Indignation welled in the eyes of the people whose gazes met mine.
“At least take back what was stolen from you with your own hands.”
As if they had been waiting for this, the Cheoldoo Group members charged at me all at once. I charged toward them, too.
“Because that’s the kind of place this world is now.”
A white flash moved, and people screamed. Then someone shouted.
“Yeah, fuck it!”
“You sons of biiitches!”
The people began to move. Every one of them had killed someone.
“M-Mom!”
“Dayoung, come here! Hold this! Do it just like you did with Mom on the subway!”
A child and their mother, too.
“You bastaaards!”
There was an older, middle-aged person, too.
“You little shits!”
But it was a hopelessly unequal fight.
The Cheoldoo Group and the remaining people were roughly equal in number, and the gang members, who had earned coins by hunting humans, were overwhelmingly stronger in combat.
That would have been the case if I hadn’t been there.
Shhkk!

The arms and legs of several Cheoldoo Group members who charged at me went flying. The chilling sensation of cutting through human flesh traveled up into my hand. The incapacitated gang members looked up at me.
At that moment.
Someone rushed past me and drove a sword straight into the mouth of a fallen Cheoldoo Group member.
“I said I’d kill them.”
[All evolution conditions for the attribute ‘Crouching Figure’ have been fulfilled.]
[The attribute of the character ‘Jung Heewon’ is blooming.]
A dazzlingly beautiful radiance was rising from her body.
I nodded.
Now it was time.
[The attribute of the character ‘Jung Heewon’ is blooming into ‘Judge of Evil (Hero).’]
Judge of Evil (滅惡). The strongest of the three great Judge attributes had just awakened from its crouch.
[You have made a major contribution to the blooming of the attribute ‘Crouching Figure’!]
[From now on, the character ‘Jung Heewon’ will not hesitate to become your sword.]
“You can rest now.”
Jung Heewon spoke, a vivid blue light flickering in her eyes.
“These bastards are mine.”
[The character ‘Jung Heewon’ is activating the exclusive skill ‘Hour of Judgement.’]
[Constellations of the Absolute Good alignment consent to the use of this skill.]
[‘Hour of Judgement’ has been activated.]
With a blood-red aura enveloping her entire body, Jung Heewon’s sword traced chilling arcs. Her kendo (劍道) wove lightly and precisely through the Cheoldoo Group. Blood sprayed everywhere.
“Aaargh!”

A scene of outright slaughter. Of course, Jung Heewon wasn’t the only one fighting. Yoo Sangah, Lee Hyunsung, and even Lee Gilyoung were holding their respective positions. But no one was as aggressive as Jung Heewon.
As if she had been born to murder, Jung Heewon killed and killed again.
When I cut off someone’s arm, Jung Heewon pierced their heart. When I cut off someone’s leg, Jung Heewon cut off their head.
Jung Heewon took care of all the unfinished work I left behind.
Without the slightest hesitation, as if she had longed for nothing but this moment for a very long time.
Our surroundings filled with blood.

Before long, Cheon Inho was the only member of the Cheoldoo Group left. Even he had been pierced all over by the civilians’ attacks. Jung Heewon looked at me, and I nodded. Cheon Inho looked at me and gave a nasty smile.
“Heh, hehehe··· Y-you······.”
He never managed to finish. Jung Heewon appeared behind him and drove her sword down through his face from the crown of his head.
[All constellations in the channel feel intense ecstasy.]
With that, everyone stopped moving.
The fight was over.
But no one could really feel that it was over.
As if all those moments until just a little while ago—sharing roasted meat, feeling that life had meaning, walking along making silly jokes, enjoying peace, however briefly—had been a lie.
Inside this goddamn scenario.
Yoo Sangah was crying.
Lee Gilyoung had his eyes closed.
Lee Hyunsung was biting his lip until it bled.
And Jung Heewon, her stamina completely spent, sat slumped in a pool of blood.
Yes, this was the truth of this world.
[Survival fees are being settled.]
The sounds of something bursting came from all around.
Those who had obtained coins survived.
Those who hadn’t obtained coins died.
And no one had been able to save anyone else.
I spoke to the people.
“Get up, everyone.”
Even if you raised your head, you couldn’t see the sky from here. As if defying some immense fate, I glared for a long time at that unseen sky.
Even the noisy constellations gave no answer this time.
“Because the scenarios have only just begun.”
While everyone was deeply stirred, I alone thought about the next scenario. As if turning a page and moving on to another chapter, my mind was simply quiet.
I had obtained everything I needed to obtain at Geumho Station.
The next stage was Chungmuro.
By the following morning, several things had changed at Geumho Station.
First, Han Myungoh had disappeared.

Han Myungoh had become hard to spot around the time the fighting began, and afterward he had vanished somewhere. Even I couldn’t tell whether he had moved on to the next station or was still hiding somewhere in this one.
“I suppose he doesn’t want to travel with us anymore. I didn’t like him from the start. Besides, he isn’t the only one who disappeared.”
Jung Heewon was right. After yesterday’s fight, hardly anyone remained at Geumho Station.
It wasn’t because few had survived. On the contrary, more people had survived than in any regression round in the original novel.
But most of the survivors had left the station after last night’s events. They probably each had their reasons.
“···Will the people who are left be all right?”
Yoo Sangah asked, looking toward the survivors.
Me, Yoo Sangah, Lee Hyunsung, Lee Gilyoung, and Jung Heewon. Apart from the five of us, only five people were still at the station.
Jung Heewon spoke first.
“Hey, you there. Are you coming with us?”
Her casually tossed question caused a considerable stir among them. A young woman holding a child’s hand stepped forward to speak for the group.
“···We’ll go separately. We still have some coins left, too.”
I was honestly impressed that the mother and daughter had survived that bloody fight. With that much courage, they might well be able to survive without joining us.
Jung Heewon seemed to think the same, because she nodded.
“All right. I wish you luck.”
When Jung Heewon turned away, relief spread across their faces.
Their reaction wasn’t really strange. What had happened yesterday had certainly been rather shocking.

I understood. One of us had refused to give alms, and the other had mercilessly slaughtered people, even if she had a reason. To them, Jung Heewon and I might not seem much different from the Cheoldoo Group.
I nudged Lee Hyunsung, who was standing beside me with a vacant expression.
“Lee Hyunsung-ssi?”
“Ah, yes!”
Lee Hyunsung, who had been staring blankly at Jung Heewon, looked startled at my voice. I thought I knew what had been on his mind.
No doubt he was wondering whether she really was the same woman who had been consumed by madness and killed the Cheoldoo Group yesterday.
“Have you finished all the preparations?”

“Yes! They’re not quite perfect, but I’ve mostly finished. I packed plastic bottles to use as canteens, made sure we have things to keep us warm, and found something suitable to use in place of an emergency mess tin······.”
Soldiers really were useful at times like these.
“······And that concludes the preparations. If there’s anything else you need······.”
There couldn’t possibly be anything else we needed······ or so I was about to say, when something suddenly came to mind.
“Oh, could you look for a portable power bank, if there is one?”
“A battery, you mean? Why would you······?”
Of course he would find that strange. A smartphone was useless when we couldn’t even get a signal. I gave a vague excuse.
“I have a use for it.”
Lee Hyunsung said he would look and began rummaging through the belongings the Cheoldoo Group had left behind. Lee Gilyoung and Yoo Sangah volunteered to help. Jung Heewon looked at me and asked,
“We’re leaving now, right?”
“We should.”

She took it for granted, without even asking whether she could come along. That was probably just the kind of person Jung Heewon was. I welcomed it, too. The ‘Judge of Evil’ was someone even Yoo Joonghyuk would covet.
“I have a lot of questions.”
“Not right now.”
“Honestly, you’re a brick wall.”
Jung Heewon lightly punched me and smiled.
[You have received 1500 coins from the character ‘Jung Heewon.’]
“What’s this······?”
“Your share. I felt bad keeping it all to myself. I gave some to the others, too.”
I quickly understood what she meant.
Yesterday, Jung Heewon had killed most of the Cheoldoo Group herself. In other words, these coins had belonged to those bastards.
But······ to be honest, I felt a little uneasy accepting them.
“I wouldn’t have shared them.”
Jung Heewon wouldn’t know. That I had actually pocketed even more coins.
“Well, I’m not you, Dokja-ssi, am I?”
She punched my arm a few more times, shouldered her backpack, and began walking toward the tunnel.
“Finish up and catch up with me. I’ll go ahead and clear things out a little.”
“Don’t get too far ahead. Some stretches are dangerous on your own.”
Jung Heewon, walking away and waving a hand as if to tell me not to worry.
[The constellation, ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire,’ likes your camaraderie.]
[The constellation, ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon,’ laughs slyly.]
I watched the messages floating in the air with an expressionless face, then spoke.
‘You made a lot yesterday, didn’t you? Good for you.’
No answer. I spoke once more.
‘Stop playing innocent and answer. I know you’re watching.’
[Ah, hahaha······ You caught me?]
It was Bihyung’s voice.
‘How much did you make?’
I silently glared into the air.
[Sigh, honestly. How did you figure it out again······? You never let anything slide. Here.]
[The dokkaebi ‘Bihyung’ has given you 4500 coins.]
Just as I’d thought.
That goddamn dokkaebi bastard.
[······The constellations sent them directly to me instead of using the sponsorship system. I don’t know why. They told me to pass them on later. Oh, and these messages, too.]
Messages bursting into view one after another.
[The constellation, ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband,’ is satisfied with your scenario.]
[The constellation, ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire,’ makes an effort to accept your judgement.]
[The constellation, ‘Secretive Plotter,’ is pleased with your scheme.]
So that was why no sponsorship messages had appeared yesterday.
After something so momentous, I had been wondering why my earnings were lower than expected.
[Coins held : 23050 C]
Even after investing a considerable portion of my previous earnings in stats, I had accumulated quite a lot of coins again.
That meant it was nearly time to raise my stats once more.
Well then, shall I give them another modest boost?
Since my Attributes Window wouldn’t open, I had to remember exactly what levels I had raised my stats to.
First······ the all-important Constitution.
[You have invested 1200 coins in Constitution.]
[Constitution Lv.12 -> Constitution lv.15]
[Your body’s durability increases!]
Since I didn’t have a separate passive attack skill, I would give Strength a solid boost, too.
[You have invested 1600 coins in Strength.]
[Strength Lv.11 -> Strength Lv.15]
[Tremendous strength surges through your muscles!]
Just enough Agility to dodge reasonably well.
[You have invested 400 coins in Agility.]
[Agility Lv.10 -> Agility Lv.11]
[You can now move a little more nimbly.]
I needed to sustain White Pure Star Energy, so I had to get Magic Power up to 10, too.
[You have invested 1200 coins in Magic Power.]
[Magic Power Lv. 6 -> Magic Power Lv.10]
[A mysterious energy settles within your soul.]
I could have raised them even further, but deliberately chose not to. Once I reached Chungmuro, there would be another place to spend a large amount of coins.
Besides, what I’d just spent already totaled 4400 coins······.
Hard to earn, easy to spend—the saying was entirely true. If my starting stats had been a little better, I wouldn’t have needed to spend this many coins.
A starting Constitution of 1······ Even the view count of Ways of Survival—no, even Lee Gilyoung’s Constitution would have been higher than that.
[Oh, I forgot······ you got two more scenario recommendations, too. You really were incredible. At this rate, I think the channel could level up soon.]
‘It had better.’
Since I couldn’t receive a sponsor’s support like other incarnations, I needed to gather even more coins.
The reason I still wasn’t getting the full benefit of my contract with Bihyung was that his channel was small.
‘A few’ constellations weren’t enough. To collect coins in earnest, I needed to build a channel that would attract at least ‘a considerable number’ of constellations.
Once we reached Chungmuro, the conditions would soon be in place.
“If everyone’s ready, let’s set out. You haven’t forgotten anything, have you?”
My companions, who had gathered by then, nodded. Judging by their tense faces, they all seemed to have learned something from yesterday’s events.
At last, our journey to Chungmuro began.
The system message appeared when we were about halfway along the tracks toward Yaksu.
[The second main scenario is being activated.]
<Main Scenario # 2 ― Meeting>
Category : Main
Difficulty : E
Clear Conditions : Pass through the tunnel and meet a survivor at the first base area.
Time Limit : None
Reward : 500 coins
Failure : ???
Seeing the message made it feel as if things were beginning in earnest. Unlike the first main scenario, the second and subsequent main scenarios had ‘major base areas.’ Jung Heewon asked,
“A major base area? Where would that be?”
There was no need to answer. Another message immediately appeared in the air.
[The next ‘major base’ is ‘Chungmuro.’]
“Chungmuro isn’t far, is it? We only need to go three more stops······.”
Normally, that would have been true.
Rrrrrrumble!
Ground rats burrowed their way into view. A pack of more than 30 ground rats. Jung Heewon’s expression hardened.
“······We have to go through this for three whole stops.”
Lee Hyunsung stepped forward without being asked.
“I’ll take the front.”

With his sponsor’s support, Lee Hyunsung’s Constitution, Strength, and Agility now totaled an impressive 37. He had earned far fewer coins than I had, yet he was catching up to me this closely······ High starting stats really did offer plenty of advantages.
If I’d known this would happen, I would at least have done some push-ups regularly.
“I’ll cover the rear, hyung.”
Lee Gilyoung’s overall stats were still low, but through consistent skill training, he had learned to use [Diverse Communication] more flexibly.
“You can count on me, too.”

Yoo Sangah was using threads made of magic power to immobilize the ground rats. She had less offensive power, but judging solely by her overall stats, I thought she might be about on par with Jung Heewon.
Crunch!
“······There are a lot of them, but they’re less trouble than I expected.”
Finally, there was really no need to say anything about Jung Heewon.
Her overall stats were lower than Lee Hyunsung’s, but her exclusive skill alone was more than enough to make her overpowered.
‘Hour of Judgement,’ the exclusive skill of the ‘Judge of Evil.’
As long as the opponent before her was an ‘evil person’ who, in the constellations’ judgement, committed clear injustice (不義), Jung Heewon would never lose.
Shhk―Yelp!
The last ground rat collapsed on the floor. Lee Hyunsung, who stood nearby holding his shield, wiped away his sweat and spoke.
“Whew······ I think we can manage this.”
In fact, this wasn’t supposed to be a difficulty level we could clear so easily.
However simple the ground rats’ attack patterns were, 30 of them was by no means a trivial number.
Even I wasn’t confident I could wipe them out alone without activating [Bookmark]. That was how much stronger my companions had become.
How much farther had we advanced through the tunnel? At last, a new platform appeared before us.
“It’s Yaksu Station. But······ there’s no one here? No, that’s not quite right.”
Yaksu Station was full of dead people and ground rat corpses. Judging by their wounds, some seemed to have fallen to Yoo Joonghyuk rather than the ground rats.
“Let’s keep going. We have two stops left now.”
We continued onward.
Since the straight-line distance from Yaksu to Dongdaeipgu Station was less than 1 km anyway, I intended to cover as much ground as possible while we could.
When we were almost at Dongdaeipgu Station, we encountered another pack of ground rats and fought them off.
In terms of distance, we had only traveled a little over 2 km in total, but the fighting was so exhausting that my companions’ stamina was dropping rapidly.
“Let’s rest here for a moment before moving on.”
“Whew······ There’s only one stop left anyway. Wouldn’t it be better to get there and rest······?”
“No one knows whether we’ll be able to rest when we get there.”
My words silenced them. Monsters certainly weren’t the only danger in this world.
I looked around for a moment, then spoke.
“It looks like the people at this station left in a hurry. They may have left behind some everyday necessities.”
“Oh, um. Then······.”

At the words ‘everyday necessities,’ Yoo Sangah raised her hand slightly. Her eyes met Jung Heewon’s. Without exchanging a word, the two nodded at the same time. As I stood there blankly, Jung Heewon asked,
“What is it? Do you want to know, too, Dokja-ssi?”
Yoo Sangah went deathly pale.
“······Heewon-ssi?”
“Ahaha, I’m joking, just joking. Of course I’m not telling him.”
···So it was a secret between women.
After they’d said that much, it would have been stranger if I hadn’t understood what they meant.
Even with the world in this state, human bodily functions didn’t stop.
Just then, Lee Hyunsung spoke up as well.
“Ah, then I’ll take this chance to rest and visit the restroom, too.”
Going to the restroom at a time like this? For a moment, I wondered what he was talking about. But on reflection, there was no reason not to use a perfectly intact restroom.
This was why the subway was so convenient.
“I’ll go with you.”
And Lee Gilyoung, too. As I watched the two walk away side by side, they looked like affectionate brothers with a large age gap.
Yoo Sangah looked at me and asked,
“Are you going to stay here alone, Dokja-ssi?”
“I’m going up to the surface for a moment.”
“What? There should be poisonous fog outside······ Will you be all right?”
“I’ll only be gone for a moment.”
At my words, Jung Heewon narrowed her eyes.
“······That sounds suspicious. You’re not going off to get something good all for yourself, are you, Dokja-ssi?”
I looked at Jung Heewon for a moment, then told her,
“It’s a secret between men.”
A short while later, I stood in front of Exit 6 of Dongdaeipgu Station.
According to the information I'd read beforehand, this was definitely the place······.
[You have been exposed to highly poisonous fog.]
As expected, the Corpse-Poison Rhinoceros's influence seemed to reach even here.
Since I hadn't purchased [Ellain Monkey’s Lungs] this time, I had to get this done quickly.
Holding my breath, I ran up the escalator leading to Dongguk University.
Before long, a statue with a bluish-gray sheen came into view.
[A constellation draped in a straw mat expresses anticipation at your actions.]

The statue was modeled after a monk who had lived during the middle of the Joseon period. The monk wore an old robe and held a large bamboo staff, and even in statue form, his face had an indefinable air of dignity.
I checked the name written vertically beneath the statue.
惟政四溟大師像
Statue of Master Yujeong Samyeongdang
Good, this was it. No sign that anyone had come here yet, either······.
Standing before the statue, I pressed my palms together.
[A constellation draped in a straw mat is pleased by your actions.]
[You have received a donation of 100 coins.]
Then, without hesitation, I activated ‘Blade of Faith’ using White Pure Star Energy.
[A constellation draped in a straw mat is puzzled by your actions.]
And just like that, I brought the blade down on the statue of Samyeongdang.
[A constellation draped in a straw mat is appalled by your actions.]
A few minutes later, I was back down in Dongdaeipgu Station, noisily tearing into some ground rat meat. I was trying to heal the skin contaminated by the highly poisonous fog.
It took a little time, but this level of contamination could be healed simply by eating the meat of an underground species.
[······Hey! Have you lost your mind? What have you been going around doing?]
And right now, Bihyung's voice was ringing in my ears, furiously berating me.
‘Shut up.’

[No, fuck, this isn't something I can just let slide. Destroying a constellation's idol like that! Do you want to see the channel go under? If that ‘Bald General of Justice’ starts bad-mouthing us······!]
A constellation's idol (偶像). Every world had constellations, and Korea was no exception.
But seriously, ‘Bald General of Justice (義兵將)’ as a modifier? He was still a great figure in Korean history, so that seemed a bit much······.
Though I wasn't really in a position to say that.
[A constellation draped in a straw mat is enraged by your atrocity.]
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ snickers.]
Every idol contained a constellation's sealed power, though the amount varied.
If an idol's seal was broken in the proper way, an incarnation body had a certain chance of obtaining the powers that constellation had used in life—items or skills, in other words.
But ‘breaking the seal’ took a long time, and there was no guarantee I'd get the skill I wanted that way.
I looked at the text file of Ways of Survival open on my smartphone.
「“But the statue of Samyeongdang should have been sealed. How did you get the skill?”
“There's a saying: if you meet the Buddha, kill the Buddha.”
“What? Don't tell me you······.”
“Haha, I just tried it to see what would happen, and it worked. ······It's true, though, isn't it? Statues are all a form of idol worship.”
“Hey! Everyone, watch out for this bastard. A constellation must have cursed them.”」
Samyeongdang's ‘skill’ was essential at the final hurdle before entering Chungmuro.
And the surest way to get the ‘skill’: destroying the idol itself.
Of course, I could buy something similar from the ‘Dokkaebi Bag’······ but the more coins I saved, the better.
“So, did you take care of that ‘secret between men’?”
I quickly turned off my smartphone's screen. Jung Heewon and the others had gathered around me before I knew it.
“Yes. And I have something for you all.”
I fumbled inside my clothes and took out the items I'd brought back. Luckily for me, Samyeongdang's idol had spat out items as well as a skill.
[Samyeongdang's Beads]
[Samyeongdang's Straw Mat]
A ragged robe and some old prayer beads. Questions filled my companions' eyes. I could guess what they were thinking.
But they needed to know this. That in this world, the ‘older’ something was, the more likely it was to be ‘excellent.’
“They may not look it, but they're good items. They belonged to a great historical figure.”
“A great historical figure?”
“Have you heard of Samyeongdang?”
[A constellation draped in a straw mat pauses at your actions.]
Jung Heewon asked with a dumb look on her face.
“······Who's that?”
[A constellation draped in a straw mat is aghast at the character ‘Jung Heewon.’]
“Oh! I know him!”
Fortunately, someone knew who he was. Needless to say, it was Yoo Sangah.
“I remember reading about him when I was studying for my Korean history certification! He was a monk during the middle of the Joseon period, right?”
“Yes, that's right.”
“He fought the Japanese forces during the Imjin War to defend the Korean Peninsula······ The Battle of Nowonpyeong and the Battle of Ugwandong!”
That was Yoo Sangah for you. I'd studied Korean history too, but I didn't know that much.
[A constellation draped in a straw mat is moved by the person ‘Yoo Sangah.’]
I nodded and said,
“In any case, these items contain his power.”
“······Really?”
“What the—it's true!”
After checking the item information, Jung Heewon and Lee Hyunsung looked astonished.
“But how did you know about these and get them, Dokja-ssi?”
“I just pressed my palms together before Samyeongdang's statue on the off chance······ and these things fell from the sky.”
“What? Surely that couldn't······.”
Even I thought it was utter bullshit, but people always had a reason for spouting nonsense.
Looking at my companions, I continued in a deliberately solemn tone.
“I think······ perhaps Samyeongdang-nim sent these to us for Korea's sake.”
My companions' ‘ah’ carried a lot of meaning. I did my best to ignore it and continued. These words weren't meant for human ears anyway.

“Perhaps he has given us the belongings he left behind to save the country once again, just as he did during the Imjin War. After all, what Korea is going through now is much like a national crisis (國亂).”
[A constellation draped in a straw mat is deeply moved by your eloquence.]
And swindlers always flourished during a national crisis.
“······With the world as it is, something like that wouldn't be so strange. Perhaps Samyeongdang-nim is one of the ‘constellations’ too. Right?”

Surprisingly, Yoo Sangah was the first to seem convinced. Perhaps she'd spoken up to spare me any embarrassment. The funny thing was that as soon as Yoo Sangah agreed, simple-minded Lee Hyunsung immediately accepted it too.
“Just as I'd expect of Samyeongdang-nim······.”
Perhaps a fresh surge of patriotism had come over him, because Lee Hyunsung looked ready to recite the Army Service Creed on the spot. Lee Gilyoung seemed fascinated too.
Only Jung Heewon was giving me a sidelong look as if to say it was nonsense.
[A constellation draped in a straw mat reveals his modifier.]
[The constellation ‘Bald General of Justice’ forgives your sin.]
I looked up at the sky with an expression that said, ‘Satisfied now?’ Bihyung looked dumbfounded.
Constellations' power and wealth were directly tied to their fame. That was why all constellations loved having their stories spread like this.
What constellation wouldn't enjoy being openly praised?
“I'll give the prayer beads to Yoo Sangah-ssi, since she knew who Samyeongdang was.”
“Really? Is it all right for me to take them?”
“I think Samyeongdang-nim would be pleased to have you use them, Yoo Sangah-ssi.”

In truth, [Samyeongdang's Beads] weren't particularly powerful for something a constellation had used. Not everything a constellation used became a Star Relic, and the fact that Samyeongdang wasn't renowned worldwide had probably played a part too.
Still, they were a B-grade item, with increased Magic Power recovery and an additional effect that boosted resistance to demons.
Jung Heewon spoke from nearby, looking at Yoo Sangah as if envious.
“Must be nice to know so much, Yoo Sangah-ssi. I didn't go to school much, so I don't know things like that.”
“Ah··· um··· well.”
“I'm joking, joking. Don't make that face.”
I spoke to the now-pouting Jung Heewon.
“There's something for you too, Jung Heewon-ssi.”
“For me too? You're going to give me that straw mat?”
“Yes.”
“No thanks. No matter how desperate I get, I'm not wearing that.”
“······Come on, try it on. I'm sure you won't regret it.”
After hesitating briefly, Jung Heewon carefully draped the straw mat over herself. She was trying to look stylish in her own way, but honestly, from any angle, she just looked like a beggar in rags.
[A constellation who likes keeping everything to themselves condemns your actions.]
[A constellation who praises fellowship approves of your actions.]
If the Star Relic [Samyeongdang's Bamboo Stick] had dropped, I would have kept it for myself, of course. But I didn't need the other two items right now.
After studying her reflection from different angles in the platform screen doors, Jung Heewon spoke with a somewhat conflicted expression.
“It's hard to explain··· but all of a sudden, I'm overflowing with a sense of justice.”

[Samyeongdang's Straw Mat] was an item that heightened an incarnation's sense of justice and willpower. I had little use for it, but it would be quite useful for Jung Heewon, who was passionate about everything.
“You said Samyeongdang, right? I feel kind of bad. I should've studied harder too.”
[The constellation ‘Bald General of Justice’ watches the situation with satisfaction.]
[You have received a donation of 100 coins.]
I said jokingly,
“Then why don't you go pay your respects with your palms together?”
It had been a joke, but Jung Heewon actually went and paid her respects with her palms together.
Poisoned by her exposure to the [Highly Poisonous Fog], Jung Heewon spoke beside me as she busily tore into some ground rat meat.
“······But someone had smashed the whole thing. You didn't do that, did you, Dokja-ssi?”
“······Dokja-ssi?”
“Anyway, let's start getting ready. We're almost at Chungmuro.”
I spoke as I looked into the pitch-black tunnel.
We had already spent some 20 minutes making our way safely forward, step by step, using Lee Gilyoung's [Diverse Communication].
Considering that the straight-line distance from Dongdaeipgu to Chungmuro was less than 1 km, it was about time for ‘that’ to appear.
[A new sub-scenario has arrived!]
Sure enough, it happened as soon as I thought of it.
“Everyone, step back.”
<Sub-Scenario ― Phantom Prison>
Category : Sub
Difficulty : D~F
Clear Conditions : Escape the Phantom Prison within the time limit.
Time Limit : 1 hour
Reward : 300 coins
Failure : ???
[Sub-scenario― ‘Phantom Prison’ has begun!]
Even that ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’ had probably struggled quite a bit with this scenario.
This scenario was one of the most dangerous traps for a regressor, after all.
Yoo Sangah asked,
“Phantom Prison? What could that be?”
She'd find out without having to ask.
“It's coming. Everyone, keep your wits about you.”

Before I'd even finished speaking, masses of something like whitish fog came rushing toward us. The fog filled the tunnel, cutting off our view in an instant. I couldn't even see my companions right beside me. Wherever I looked, nothing but scenery distorted as if I were on drugs.
“Aagh······ This feels awful!”
Jung Heewon screamed. She was probably seeing something different from what I was seeing.
「Dokja.」
A voice I didn't want to hear. The voice of someone I'd long forgotten reached me through a landscape like a drug-induced hallucination. If it was this bad for me, it would be worse for the others.
“······Something feels strange. Dokja-ssi! Are you there?”
“Dokja-ssi! Dokja-ssi!”
Amid my distorted vision, my companions' voices were gradually receding.
[Phantom Prison].
A space that preyed on people's trauma and drove them to madness.
「Dokja, you didn't see anything. Understand?」
The scenery blurs, and someone's face emerges.
I stared silently into empty space, then smiled bitterly. As if denying that this was real.
[The exclusive skill ‘Fourth Wall’ activates!]
[The skill's effect grants immunity to ‘Phantom Prison.’]
As my mind relaxed, the unsettling sensation faded.
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ admires your mental fortitude.]
[You have received a donation of 100 coins.]
[A curious constellation regrets being unable to peek into your memories.]
As the Phantom Prison's power weakened, I sensed presences around me.
“Everyone, calm down and take slow, deep breaths.”

Those trapped in the Phantom Prison lost their reason and unleashed their madness on everything around them. That made the companions beside you the most dangerous thing in the Phantom Prison. Concern over this prison might also have been one reason Yoo Joonghyuk had set out alone.
“P-Private Lee Hyunsung. Could you repeat that?”
“I'm sorry. I'm sorry, Mom!”
“You··· you fucking bastards!”
······Was I already too late? I heard my companions' anguished cries as madness engulfed them. But it hadn't taken all of them.
“······Dokja-ssi?”
Just then, Yoo Sangah appeared within the Phantom Prison. [Samyeongdang's Beads] around her wrist were glowing brightly. Fortunately, they had worked.
I approached Yoo Sangah and said,
“Please cover the area around us. I'm going to destroy this space now.”
Yoo Sangah nodded, her expression tense.
[Activating exclusive skill, ‘Destroy Evil (破魔) Lv.1.’]
Destroy Evil (破魔). A skill one tier above Repel Evil (退魔), which could be purchased with coins. This skill was the very reason I'd gone out of my way to smash Samyeongdang's statue.
[Exclusive skill, ‘Destroy Evil Lv.1,’ dispels ‘Phantom Prison.’]
Sure enough, the effect was immediate—perhaps because it was a skill Samyeongdang had used. If I'd purchased Repel Evil, dispelling it would have taken at least a minute.
Ssshh.
As the fog receded and the Phantom Prison vanished, my companions came into view one by one.
“O-Our resolve! We are the Republic of Korea Army, loyal to our nation and its people!”
The sight made their traumas clear at a glance. Lee Hyunsung lay facedown with his head pressed to the floor, while Lee Gilyoung trembled with his head buried against his knees.
Yoo Sangah stepped forward first.
“Hyunsung-ssi? Gilyoung! Everyone, snap out of it!”
Just then, a blade came blindly swinging at us from behind. Fortunately, it wasn't moving fast, so it wasn't difficult to dodge.
“······I'll kill them all.”
Jung Heewon was holding her sword aloft, glaring into empty space like a madwoman.
My heart sank as I watched her eyes gradually turn red.
This was dangerous. It was a sign of [Demon Slaying].
Thwack!
I struck the back of Jung Heewon's neck hard with the edge of my hand, knocking her unconscious. Fortunately, she went down immediately.
I'd even given her [Samyeongdang's Straw Mat] in case something like this happened, but her mental state seemed more fragile than I'd thought.
“Yoo Sangah-ssi, please look after Jung Heewon-ssi.”
“It isn't over yet.”
[You have fulfilled the sub-scenario's clear conditions!]
[You have obtained 300 coins!]
As soon as the clear message appeared, monsters emerged before my eyes. Strange, gelatinous creatures whose forms resembled ectoplasm (Ectoplasm).
Grade-8 ghost species, Specters.
This group of Specters was responsible for creating the [Phantom Prison]. I used White Pure Star Energy to activate ‘Blade of Faith.’
Shhk!
Skreeee!
Fortunately, the fight itself wasn't difficult. Specters weren't difficult monsters to deal with as long as you could break through their ‘Phantom Prison.’
With eerie shrieks, all the Specters vanished.
[Specter's Stone].
I put the dropped spirit stones into my pocket. I needed to collect these too.
Perhaps thanks to Yoo Sangah, my companions were quickly regaining their senses.
“Is everyone all right?”
As expected, simple-minded Lee Hyunsung recovered the fastest. After hearing what had happened, he sighed and bowed his head.
“······Thank you. That could have ended very badly. I'm in your debt again, Dokja-ssi.”
“Not at all.”
“My head hurts······.”
Lee Gilyoung kept tapping his head. I gently cradled it in my hands. He was pretending to be all right, but this child probably had the most horrific trauma of anyone here.
I could see a faint light coming from the distance. Yoo Sangah said,
“Dokja-ssi, I think we're here.”
I thought it over for a moment. Jung Heewon was unconscious, and the others were in no condition to fight at full strength.
Would it be all right to enter like this?
But someone else settled my dilemma for me.
A blade suddenly emerging from the darkness. But the movement was purely a threat, with no intent to hurt us.
“Who are you people? Don't you know this area is our hunting ground?”
A girl holding a long sword (長刀) stood at the entrance where the faint light came in. A youthful face that looked about seventeen, and a familiar girls' high school uniform.
She wore a zip-up hoodie as if to conceal her name tag, but it couldn't conceal her striking looks.
“Oh, that girl is······!”
Sharp-eyed Yoo Sangah was the first to recognize her.
I knew her too.
Because she was also one of the novel's major supporting characters.
The sole survivor of Taepung Girls' High School, Lee Jihye.
She was one of the reasons Yoo Joonghyuk had pushed himself to head straight to Chungmuro in the shortest time possible.
“······Did you people just kill the Specters?”
Lee Jihye looked startled when she noticed the spirit stone in my hand.
“How on earth······ Isn't my master the only one who can kill those things?”
I immediately activated my skill.
